public_rationale: Part holds. DeepSeek's models existed and worked. An independent developer-tool maker reported in January 2025 that V3 matched Claude 3.5 Sonnet on simple tasks, though it was weaker on complex work. Against peer flagship models, DeepSeek was far cheaper. R1 was about 27 times cheaper than o1, and V3 was about 18 to 54 times cheaper than GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet. That is more than one order of magnitude. But the claim is broader than that. It says DeepSeek's models were 'magnitudes cheaper' than models from the hyperscalers and from OpenAI and Anthropic. OpenAI's GPT-4o mini cost about the same as V3's discounted price ($0.15 vs $0.14 input) and less than V3's full price. Google's Gemini 1.5 Flash, at $0.075 input and $0.30 output, was cheaper than V3 on input. So the price part fails for Google's Gemini, which he names, and for the budget models of OpenAI and Anthropic.
limitations: If the claim is read as peer models only, the OpenAI and Anthropic price part is supported, and the Gemini point rests on a pre-period price.
The independent performance evidence is anecdotal rather than a formal benchmark.

statement.excerpt: DeepSeek’s models actually exist, they work (at least, by the standards of hallucination-prone LLMs that don’t, at the risk of repeating myself, know anything in the true meaning of the word), they've been independently verified to be competitive in performance, and they are magnitudes cheaper in price than those from both hyperscalers (EG: Google's Gemini, Meta's Llama, Amazon Q, etc.) and from OpenAI and Anthropic.

our_interpretation: 'DeepSeek's models' means V3 and R1, the models discussed in the post.
'Magnitudes cheaper' is read as at least about ten times cheaper per token in API list prices. The plural suggests more.

The comparison set as written is models from the hyperscalers (Gemini is named) and from OpenAI and Anthropic. The test is whether DeepSeek was that much cheaper across those providers' offerings, and at minimum against their peer models.
'Independently verified competitive' is read as third-party testing finding performance broadly comparable to leading models.
The period runs from V3's release (2024-12-26) to the post date (2025-01-29).
criteria.support_condition: Third-party testing found DeepSeek's models competitive, and their API prices were about ten times lower or more than those of the named providers' models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Third-party testing found them clearly not competitive, or the named providers offered models priced about the same as or below DeepSeek's.
